key_insight: A reverse diode in the equivalent-circuit model explains inefficient electron extraction and S-shaped current–voltage curves in valley photovoltaic devices.
engineering_relevance: Eliminating reverse-diode behavior is necessary for valley photovoltaic devices to achieve high efficiency.
method: Measure intensity- and voltage-dependent photoluminescence and electrical responses.
Model both responses with a shared equivalent circuit.
Use Poisson/drift-diffusion simulations to investigate the reverse diode’s physical origin.
evidence_signal: The equivalent circuit captures the measured S-shaped current–voltage curves while simultaneously describing photoluminescence and electrical measurements.
watch_item: The reverse diode could arise from valley scattering or a heterojunction barrier, so its physical origin must be distinguished before choosing a mitigation strategy.
paper_title: Combined photoluminescence and electrical characterization of valley photovoltaic devices explained with an equivalent circuit
